docs.title: MeshCore RAK9154 battery telemetry
docs.text:
Firmware for the RAK4631 MeshCore repeater that reads the real battery data from a RAK9154 Solar Battery (Output 1, RAK SensorHub one-wire) and reports it through MeshCore's normal telemetry, instead of the default 0.0 V.

Download the latest firmware Source and README

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
Telemetry channel Value Channel 1 Battery voltage, state of charge (%), charge current Next channel Battery temperature

The stock RAK_4631_repeater build is unchanged. The new build is the separate target RAK_4631_repeater_RAK9154.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Open the latest release and download RAK_4631_repeater_RAK9154-<version>.zip.
  2. Flash it to the RAK4631 as a DFU package (for example with the Adafruit nRF52 bootloader / nRF Connect).
  3. On the repeater console run rak9154 status. A working link shows voltage, current, SOC and temperature.

See the RAK9154 guide for flags, console commands, troubleshooting and limitations.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Releases are built automatically from upstream MeshCore plus this change, and are unit-tested and compiled for both targets. They are not hardware-tested for every version: flash a test node first.

docs.title: RAK9154 Battery Telemetry — Implementation Plan
docs.text: Status: research complete, Phase 1 implementation in progress. Everything below was read from source on 2026-10-18; items that could not be verified are marked UNVERIFIED.

docs.title: 1. Upstream MeshCore commit
docs.text:
• Repo: https://github.com/meshcore-dev/MeshCore, branch main
  • Commit used: 81dbae592ffad40b4212bc0b37e82b38da08f4bc ("Merge branch 'dev'", 2026-10-15)
  • License: MIT

Baseline build (RAK_4631_repeater): not completed in the authoring environment. PlatformIO's registry hosts (api.registry.platformio.org) were blocked by the sandbox egress policy, so the nordicnrf52 platform and toolchain could not be installed. The baseline must be confirmed by CI / a developer machine (see section 11). Also note sh build.sh fails on Debian/Ubuntu because /bin/sh is dash and build.sh uses bash arrays; use bash build.sh ... there (macOS sh is bash and works).

docs.title: 2. RAK4631 board class and relevant files
docs.text: Purpose Path Board class RAK4631Board : NRF52BoardDCDC variants/rak4631/RAK4631Board.h, RAK4631Board.cpp Globals (board, radio_driver, sensors, rtc_clock) variants/rak4631/target.h, target.cpp Pin map (PIN_SERIAL1_RX=15, PIN_SERIAL1_TX=16, WB_IO*) variants/rak4631/variant.h PlatformIO section [rak4631] and envs variants/rak4631/platformio.ini nRF52 base ([nrf52_base]) root platformio.ini Repeater firmware examples/simple_repeater/{main.cpp,MyMesh.cpp,MyMesh.h}

docs.title: 3. Current getBattMilliVolts()
docs.text:
variants/rak4631/RAK4631Board.h:

#define PIN_VBAT_READ    5
#define ADC_MULTIPLIER   (3 * 1.73 * 1.187 * 1000)
#define BATTERY_SAMPLES 8
uint16_t getBattMilliVolts() override {
  analogReadResolution(12);
  uint32_t raw = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < BATTERY_SAMPLES; i++) raw += analogRead(PIN_VBAT_READ);
  raw = raw / BATTERY_SAMPLES;
  return (ADC_MULTIPLIER * raw) / 4096;
}

Interface: mesh::MainBoard::getBattMilliVolts() is pure virtual, returns uint16_t (src/MeshCore.h:47). This is the only place that needs to change for Phase 1.

NRF52_POWER_MANAGEMENT (boot-voltage lockout, calls getBattMilliVolts() in NRF52Board.cpp) is not defined for the RAK4631 envs in this commit, so the cached getter returning "not available" at boot cannot trigger a boot lockout. Re-check if that ever changes.

docs.title: 4. Telemetry call path
docs.text:
• Remote telemetry request → examples/simple_repeater/MyMesh.cpp:243-259: telemetry.reset(); telemetry.addVoltage(TELEM_CHANNEL_SELF, board.getBattMilliVolts()/1000.0f); sensors.querySensors(perm_mask, telemetry);
  • Repeater stats → MyMesh.cpp:218 (stats.batt_milli_volts), also StatsFormatHelper.h:14.
  • Local/remote CLI power → src/helpers/CommonCLI.cpp:295.
  • Cayenne LPP is used (electroniccats/CayenneLPP @ 1.6.1). Voltage on TELEM_CHANNEL_SELF (=1). EnvironmentSensorManager::querySensors() appends other sensors on channels 2+.
  • No protocol change is needed for Phase 1: the voltage rides the existing field.

docs.title: 5. Architecture facts that constrain the design
docs.text:
• Main loop (examples/simple_repeater/main.cpp): cooperative, single-threaded. Per iteration: serial CLI, board.loop(), the_mesh.loop(), sensors.loop(), rtc_clock.tick(). MainBoard::loop() (MeshCore.h) is an existing, empty-by-default per-iteration hook → the natural place to run the RAK9154 service. No new scheduling mechanism is needed.
  • CLI extension: MainBoard::handleCommand(const char* command, uint32_t sender_timestamp, char* reply) is already consulted first by CommonCLI::handleCommand (CommonCLI.cpp:189). A rak9154 command can be added from the board class with no change to shared CLI code. Reply buffer is 160 bytes.
  • Hardware abstraction: mesh::MainBoard virtuals (getBattMilliVolts, isChargerActive, handleCommand, loop). isChargerActive() is reported by the power CLI command.
  • Timing: the radio is driven from the_mesh.loop(); anything slow in loop()/getBattMilliVolts() delays packet handling. The getBattMilliVolts() path must stay a pure cache read.
  • Build: build.sh wraps pio run -e <env>; platformio.ini loads variants/*/platformio.ini (single directory level).
  • BSP / deps (pinned in root platformio.ini): platform = nordicnrf52; framework-arduinoadafruitnrf52 from the MeshCore fork at commit d541301665b40959682252911e57b11df3ee651a; platformio/toolchain-gccarmnoneeabi@^1.140201.0; CayenneLPP 1.6.1; RadioLib pinned to a commit. -w (warnings off) is in the base flags.

docs.title: 6. RAK9154 — Meshtastic implementation findings
docs.text:
Files (Meshtastic firmware @ 8ebb6988b56e8da82bb56a3f55bf7908e9e5c465): src/modules/Telemetry/Sensor/RAK9154Sensor.{h,cpp}, enabled by -DHAS_RAKPROT=1.

  • Pin: HALF_UART_PIN, defined in variants/nrf52840/rak2560/variant.h as PIN_SERIAL1_RX (code comment: "P0.15"). That is the RAK2560 variant, not a RAK4631 repeater harness.
  • Serial: RAK's SoftwareHalfSerial at 9600 baud, one pin for TX and RX.
  • It delegates framing/checksum entirely to RAK-OneWireSerial (RakSNHub_Protocl_API); RAK9154Sensor.cpp itself only handles events.
  • Sequence: init() → master broadcasts a provision BOOT request → probe answers with a provision request → master replies assigning PID (ADD_PID event) → master issues one get sensor data request → afterwards the probe sends periodic report frames. A 50 ms periodic task drains the RX buffer (2 ms inter-byte timeout) and feeds process().
  • Values used (only three):
IPSO id Meaning Request-response path (SDATA_REQ) Periodic report path (REPORT) 0xB8 (3384-3200) capacity, 1 byte, % (clamped to 100) msg[1] msg[1] 0xB9 (3385-3200) DC current, 2 bytes, signed, mA little-endian (msg[2]<<8)+msg[1] big-endian (msg[1]<<8)+msg[2] 0xBA (3386-3200) DC voltage, 2 bytes, ×10 → mV little-endian big-endian

Quirk: the two Meshtastic code paths decode multi-byte values with opposite byte order. Whether this reflects real device behaviour or a bug is UNVERIFIED; the driver must treat it as an open hardware question (see section 13) and log raw bytes in RAK9154_DEBUG builds. - Charging: current > 0 is treated as charging (positive = into battery). - Error handling: checksum and sequence errors are logged only. - License: GPL-3.0 (Meshtastic LICENSE).

docs.title: 7. RAK-OneWireSerial findings
docs.text:
Repo beegee-tokyo/RAK-OneWireSerial (cloned, current default branch). Files: src/RAK-OneWireSerial.h, SoftwareHalfSerial.{h,cpp}, onewire_master_protocol.{c,h}, onewire_master_api.h.

  • README: RAK2560 SensorHub probes and IO probes, and RAK9154 Solar Battery Lite; "designed only for the WisBlock RAK4631"; preferred pin RX1 = P0.15, other GPIOs "should work but are untested"; library marked BETA.
  • library.json: MIT. But SoftwareHalfSerial.{h,cpp} carry an LGPL-2.1 header (adapted from Arduino SoftwareSerial).
  • Not consumable as a clean dependency here: it is built around global static state (record[1], menu, dataBuff), has heavy packed structs with enum members (size depends on -fshort-enums), pulls Adafruit_TinyUSB.h, bit-bangs RX inside a GPIO ISR, and has no bounds-checking on several paths ((U8)len casts, unchecked rakipso_tbl[ipso] index, unchecked payload offsets). Only a few hundred lines of protocol are actually needed, so a minimal, bounds-checked, independent implementation is preferred.

docs.title: 8. Exact protocol / frame information
docs.text:
Derived from onewire_master_protocol.c; all multi-byte header fields below were checked by tracing the code.

Serial: 9600 baud, 8N1, idle high, single wire (half duplex).

byte  0     0xFF   wakeup (ignored by receiver; library prepends it)
byte  1     0x7E   delimiter / start
byte  2..3  LEN    big-endian u16 = 6 (hub header) + hub payload_length
byte  4     TYPE   0=ECHO 1=ATCMD 2=SENSORHUB   (only 2 is accepted)
byte  5     FLAG   0=REQ 1=RSP
--- SensorHub header (6 bytes, counted in LEN) ---
byte  6     dest PID   (0x00 master, 0xFF unknown/broadcast)
byte  7     source PID
byte  8     sequence
byte  9     hub type: 0 wakeup,1 provision,2 paramset,3 senddata,4 control,5 paramget,6 alert,7 err,8 ack,9 nack,...
byte 10     payload_length
byte 11     payload type
byte 12..   payload (payload_length bytes)
last        CHECKSUM
  • Checksum (cal_chksum): popcount(TYPE) + popcount(FLAG) + Σ popcount(b) over the LEN bytes starting at byte 6, 8-bit wrap. It does not cover wakeup, delimiter, or LEN. It sits at byte 6+LEN. (Receiver also tolerates LEN == 6+payload_length-1, an old firmware quirk.)
  • Master → probe, provision BOOT: FF 7E 00 06 02 00 FF 00 <seq> 01 00 02 <chk> (13 bytes).
  • Master → probe, get data: FF 7E 00 06 02 00 <pid> 00 <seq> 03 00 02 <chk> (13 bytes). The reference library writes the checksum over the (unused) sid byte; the wire frame is the 13 bytes above.
  • Probe → master provision (hub type 1, ptype 3 "VER3"), payload: hw(1) sw(3) sn(18) provId(1) reserved(7) model(20) reserved(4) snsr_num(1) {sid(1) ipso(1) rule(2)}×snsr_num. Master must answer with the same frame, flag=RSP, dest/source swapped, provId = assigned PID (reference assigns 1), checksum recomputed.
  • Sensor data payload (hub type 3): repeated {sid(1), ipso(1), value(size[ipso])}; sizes for our fields: 0xB8:1, 0xB9:2, 0xBA:2. Flag=REQ is an unsolicited report; flag=RSP answers our get-data.
  • Candidate IDs from the task (0x15–0x1A): not found in any source read. The real IDs are the IPSO ones above. Temperature (RAK_IPSO_TEMP_SENSOR = 3303-3200 = 0x67, 2 bytes) exists in the table, but no evidence that the RAK9154 reports it; status flags: no evidence at all. Phase 2 for those fields is therefore gated on seeing a real device's provision sensor list.

docs.title: 9. Licensing assessment
docs.text:
Source License Use MeshCore MIT target license for all new code Meshtastic RAK9154Sensor.* GPL-3.0 not copied. Read only to learn observable behaviour (IDs, scaling, sequence). Facts about a wire protocol are not copyrightable expression. RAK-OneWireSerial protocol (onewire_master_*) MIT read for format; new code is independent; attribution added in docs RAK-OneWireSerial SoftwareHalfSerial.* LGPL-2.1 not copied or linked. Own half-duplex transport written from scratch using the generic bit-bang technique

This assessment is an engineering judgement, not legal advice.

docs.title: 10. GPIO / interface mapping (UNVERIFIED — configurable)
docs.text:
Evidence: RAK-OneWireSerial README (preferred RX1 = P0.15) and Meshtastic RAK2560 (HALF_UART_PIN = PIN_SERIAL1_RX) both point at P0.15 = Arduino pin 15, which is PIN_SERIAL1_RX in variants/rak4631/variant.h. I did not find a public document showing (a) the RAK9154 Output 1 connector pinout, (b) the WisMesh Repeater harness pinout, or (c) which RAK19007/RAK19026 base-board net reaches P0.15, nor signal levels or any level-shift/protection circuit. These must be checked against RAK's datasheets and a multimeter/scope before connecting.

Plan: RAK9154_ONEWIRE_PIN defaults to PIN_SERIAL1_RX (15) with a loud comment; override with -D RAK9154_ONEWIRE_PIN=<n>. Conflict: the RAK4631 env maps the GPS UART to the same pins (PIN_GPS_TX=PIN_SERIAL1_RX). The new target therefore adds -UENV_INCLUDE_GPS (same trade-off Meshtastic makes for this feature). Documented in docs/RAK9154.md.

docs.title: 11. Proposed source files and PlatformIO changes
docs.text:
New (no upstream file edited except the board class):

variants/rak4631/rak9154/RAK9154Protocol.{h,cpp}    pure C++, no Arduino: frame build/parse/checksum, decode to struct
variants/rak4631/rak9154/RAK9154Battery.{h,cpp}     state machine + cached telemetry + counters (transport injected)
variants/rak4631/rak9154/RAK9154HalfSerial.{h,cpp}  nRF52 single-wire bit-bang transport
variants/rak4631_rak9154/platformio.ini             new env (separate dir so no upstream .ini line changes)
test/test_rak9154/                                  native googletest parser/state-machine tests + fixtures
docs/RAK9154.md, docs/RAK9154-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md
.github/workflows/build-rak9154.yml

Why a second variants/ directory: extra_configs = variants/*/platformio.ini only matches one directory level, so a sibling directory holding just the new [env:...] means upstream's variants/rak4631/platformio.ini is never edited and cannot conflict on merge.

Edited upstream files (guarded by #ifdef RAK9154_BATTERY, small): - variants/rak4631/RAK4631Board.h/.cpp: include, one member, getBattMilliVolts() prefers the cached value, loop() override, handleCommand()/isChargerActive() overrides. - Root platformio.ini: add a native test env entry for the new tests (only needed if the existing [env:native] filter cannot be reused; otherwise untouched).

Env: [env:RAK_4631_repeater_RAK9154] extends env:RAK_4631_repeater, appends -D RAK9154_BATTERY, -UENV_INCLUDE_GPS, and an ADVERT_NAME. All rak9154/*.cpp are wrapped in #if defined(RAK9154_BATTERY) || defined(RAK9154_HOST_TEST) so the stock target compiles them to nothing (stock image should be byte-identical; compare sizes).

docs.title: 12. Polling / state-machine design
docs.text:
All time is passed in (loop(nowMs)), transport is an interface → host-testable.

States: INIT → PROVISIONING → POLLING (any state → PROVISIONING after repeated timeouts). - PROVISIONING: send provision BOOT broadcast, wait ≤ 250 ms (bounded) for the probe's provision request; reply with RSP assigning PID 1. Retry every poll period. - POLLING: every RAK9154_POLL_INTERVAL_MS (default 30 000, clamped 15 000–60 000) send get-data to the PID and wait ≤ 250 ms. Unsolicited reports are accepted at any time. - RX is interrupt-fed into a 64-byte ring buffer; loop() drains it non-blockingly (never waits for bytes), assembles frames with a length-prefixed state machine (max frame 64 bytes, bad length → resync on next 0x7E), then validates: delimiter, TYPE=2, LEN consistency, checksum, hub type, bounded payload walk, known IPSO sizes. - Cache updated only from fully validated frames, per-field. hasValidTelemetry() = have voltage and now - lastValid < 5 min (configurable). Getter is a few loads; never touches the wire. - Counters: ok polls, timeouts, bad checksums, invalid frames, unknown IPSO ids, provisions, last response age. Exposed via rak9154 status. - TX is the only blocking part: ≤ 13 bytes ≈ 14 ms with that one pin's interrupt masked, once per poll. This is a bounded exception to "non-blocking"; the alternative (timer/PPI-driven TX) is a candidate follow-up if bench tests show jitter.

docs.title: 13. Risks and unresolved hardware questions
docs.text:
1. GPIO / Output 1 pinout / level shifting: UNVERIFIED (section 10). Wrong pin = no data; wrong wiring could damage the GPIO.
  2. Byte order of 16-bit values differs between the two Meshtastic code paths. First bench step: capture raw frames (RAK9154_DEBUG) and compare with the multimeter voltage; decode is isolated in one function.
  3. Does the RAK9154 need the provisioning handshake, or only emit periodic reports? Driver supports both, but the real behaviour is untested.
  4. Temperature / status fields: no verified IPSO ids; Phase 2 depends on the provision sensor list from real hardware.
  5. Bit-banged RX timing can be corrupted by higher-priority interrupts (SoftDevice/USB); checksum rejects corrupted frames, and a missed frame only delays an update.
  6. GPS and the one-wire pin share P0.15 by default; GPS is disabled in the new target.
  7. PlatformIO builds not run in the authoring sandbox (registry blocked) — Phase 1 acceptance criteria 1–3 and all on-hardware criteria (4–10) are open until CI/bench confirm them.
  8. sh build.sh does not work on dash-based /bin/sh; use bash build.sh.

docs.title: RAK9154 Solar Battery telemetry (RAK4631 repeater)
docs.text:
Reads battery voltage from a RAK9154 Solar Battery Output 1 (RAK SensorHub one-wire, 9600 8N1, half duplex – not Modbus) and feeds it to MeshCore's existing battery telemetry, which otherwise reads 0.0 V on this hardware.

Everything is behind -D RAK9154_BATTERY. The stock RAK_4631_repeater target is unchanged.

docs.title: Targets
docs.text:
env description RAK_4631_repeater stock, untouched RAK_4631_repeater_RAK9154 stock + -D RAK9154_BATTERY, GPS disabled (-UENV_INCLUDE_GPS), advert name "RAK9154 Repeater"

Build: pio run -e RAK_4631_repeater_RAK9154 (or bash build.sh; note build.sh needs bash, not dash).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
RAK4631Board::loop() -> RAK9154Battery::loop()   drain RX, validate frames, update cache, send ONE request per poll
RAK4631Board::getBattMilliVolts() -> cache       O(1), never touches the wire; falls back to the stock ADC path if
                                                 there is no fresh RAK9154 reading
  • rak9154/RAK9154Protocol.* – pure framing / checksum / decode (host-testable, no hardware).
  • rak9154/RAK9154Battery.* – cache, state machine (provision -> poll), timeouts, stats, CLI text.
  • rak9154/RAK9154HalfSerial.* – bit-banged half-duplex UART on one pin (GPIOTE falling-edge RX, DWT-timed TX).
  • Poll every 30 s (clamped 15–60 s); cache is stale after 5 min; 1.5 s response timeout; re-provision after 3 timeouts.
  • Blocking: only transmitting a request (~14 ms/poll). RX is interrupt-fed (~1 ms of ISR time per received byte).

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: flag default meaning RAK9154_BATTERY off enable feature RAK9154_ONEWIRE_PIN PIN_SERIAL1_RX UNVERIFIED – see below RAK9154_DEBUG off serial log lines RAK9154_POLL_INTERVAL_MS 30000 RAK9154_STALE_MS 300000 RAK9154_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS / RAK9154_REPROVISION_AFTER 1500 / 3 the custom env uses 4000 / 10 during bring-up RAK9154_RSP_BIG_ENDIAN / RAK9154_REPORT_BIG_ENDIAN 0 / 1 UNVERIFIED 16-bit byte order RAK9154_TX_GAP_BITS 4 idle bit times after every transmitted byte (RAK's reference class spaces bytes ~12 bit times; change live with rak9154 gap <n>, 0-16, not persisted) RAK9154_RX_LATENCY_CYCLES 320 ISR entry latency used to centre sampling; tune with a scope

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: rak9154 (same as rak9154 status), rak9154 diag, rak9154 extra, rak9154 gap [n], rak9154 poll, rak9154 info, rak9154 raw [offset] (pages through the last received frame; replies are limited to ~150 characters, so use e.g. raw 35 and raw 70 for the rest). status shows validity, voltage, age and the diagnostic counters (requests, ok, timeouts, bad checksum, invalid, framing, unknown channels, range rejects).

docs.title: Pin verification (REQUIRED before connecting anything)
docs.text: The GPIO carrying Output 1 on a WisMesh repeater harness was not established from documentation. The default (P0.15) is what RAK's library and a Meshtastic RAK variant use, nothing more. Before powering: 1. Trace the RAK9154 Output 1 wire to the WisBlock slot pin with a multimeter/continuity (unpowered). 2. Find that pin's nRF52840 GPIO in the RAK4631 schematic; confirm it is not used by the radio, I2C, GPS, or LEDs. 3. Check the probe's logic level is 3.3 V before it touches an nRF52 pin. 4. Set -D RAK9154_ONEWIRE_PIN=<arduino pin> accordingly. Note the GPS option uses some of the same header pins, which is why the custom target disables GPS. 5. First power-up: scope/logic analyser on the line if possible; confirm 9600 baud idle-high frames.

docs.title: Channels decoded
docs.text:
Per RAK's RAK9154 payload decoder (that page documents the LoRaWAN uplink of a RAK2560 hub, which shares the sensor IDs; the one-wire byte order is separate and still unverified here):

IPSO field size / scale 0xBA battery voltage 2 B unsigned, 0.01 V 0xB9 battery current 2 B signed, 0.01 A (+/-1.5 A range) 0xB8 state of charge 1 B, % 0x67 temperature 2 B signed, 0.1 C (-30..105) 0xF3 battery errors and battery FW version 2 B; faults are bits 6..11: 6 over-voltage, 7 charge over-current, 8 charge low-temp, 9 charge high-temp, 10 charge short-circuit, 11 charge over-current lock

The two 0xF3 entries are told apart only by their channel byte, and RAK documents the channel only for the FW version (example 0x1A). Observed on a real probe: 0x19 = faults (0000, none) and 0x1A = firmware (0004 = V00.04). The driver stores both raw with their channels; rak9154 extra shows them, labelling a word with any bit outside 6..11 as a firmware version and 0 as "no faults". That labelling is a heuristic until it is seen on a real probe. Not published over the mesh yet.

docs.title: What appears in the app's telemetry
docs.text:
channel value source 1 battery voltage MeshCore's own getBattMilliVolts(), i.e. the cached RAK9154 value (percent in the app is the app's own estimate from the voltage) 1 state of charge RAK9154 0xB8, LPP percentage 1 charge current RAK9154 0xB9, LPP current 1 nRF52 chip temperature MeshCore default, unrelated to the battery next free channel (2 with no other sensors) battery temperature RAK9154 0x67 same channel as the battery temperature fault byte (LPP digital input, 0 = none; bit0 OV, 1 charge-OC, 2 charge-low-temp, 3 charge-high-temp, 4 charge-short, 5 charge-OC-lock) RAK9154 0xF3 fault word (bits 6..11 shifted down)

Notes: LPP "current" is unsigned, so only charging current is shown and discharge reads 0 A; the probe's sign convention is unverified (compare rak9154 status current by day and night). Battery temperature is not put on channel 1 because the chip temperature is already there and two temperatures on one channel collide in the app. Only requesters with base telemetry permission get the extras (guests see voltage only). The fault word (0xF3) is published as the fault byte; the firmware-version word stays console-only (rak9154 extra). The hook is a few lines in EnvironmentSensorManager::querySensors, guarded by RAK9154_BATTERY.

docs.title: Byte-order bench procedure
docs.text: Voltage endianness is unverified. With a battery of known voltage: run rak9154 raw and rak9154 info, compare the decoded value. A range rejects count rising means the byte order is wrong; flip RAK9154_RSP_BIG_ENDIAN / RAK9154_REPORT_BIG_ENDIAN and re-test. Please contribute real captures to test/test_rak9154/fixtures.h.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Host tests (53 protocol/driver tests + 15 simulated-hardware tests of the real transport source), ASan/UBSan: see .github/workflows/build-rak9154.yml for exact commands. The existing fixtures are synthetic, built from an independent encoder; they prove internal consistency, not agreement with a real probe.

docs.title: What has and has not been verified
docs.text:
Verified in the development sandbox: host tests; cross-compile of all new/changed sources for Cortex-M4 against the real Adafruit nRF52 headers; with the flag off the board code disassembles identically to upstream and the new sources compile to empty objects; the new env equals the stock env plus four flags.

Not verified (CI/bench needed): full PlatformIO build of both targets (registry unreachable in the sandbox), booting, any communication with a real RAK9154, the pin, byte order, whether the probe needs provisioning, RX timing margin under radio/USB interrupt load, and any temperature/status field meaning.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text: Original MIT code. No code was copied from Meshtastic (GPL-3.0) or from RAK's SoftwareHalfSerial (LGPL-2.1); the protocol was derived from reading RAK's MIT-licensed protocol sources and public descriptions. Credit: RAK Wireless SensorHub protocol documentation/library.

docs.title: Keeping up with upstream
docs.text: See the section "Keeping this fork up to date with upstream MeshCore" in the top-level README.md (merge procedure, conflict hot-spots, post-merge checklist).

docs.title: Phase 2 status
docs.text: Done: state of charge, charge current and battery temperature are published in the telemetry reply (see "What appears in the app's telemetry"). Not done: publishing the 0xF3 fault/firmware words (needs a real capture to confirm which channel is which), signed current (the LPP current type is unsigned; would need another encoding), and companion / room-server targets.
